title: Microsoft ships emergency Windows fix after shutdown bug
summary: Microsoft released out-of-band emergency updates to address regressions introduced by its January 2026 security patches, after some Windows 11 PCs couldn’t shut down or hibernate properly [engadget.com#1][ghacks.net#1][google.com#1]. The shutdown problem primarily affected Windows 11 devices using Secure Launch, where attempting to power down could trigger an unexpected restart instead [engadget.com#1][pcmag.com#1]. The same emergency release also fixes a separate issue that blocked Remote Desktop and other remote connection apps from signing in on some Windows 10 and Windows 11 systems due to credential prompt failures [engadget.com#1][ghacks.net#1].
talking_points: How it hit: PCMag reports the shutdown bug showed up for some users of Secure Launch and Microsoft provided a temporary fix path to restore normal power behavior [pcmag.com#1].
Remote login: Microsoft tied the remote-connection failures to problems displaying or handling credential prompts when logging in via remote apps on affected Windows 10/11 devices [engadget.com#1].
More reports: Separate reporting highlighted claims of Nvidia GeForce performance issues after the January update, adding to user-reported regressions around the patch cycle [google.com#1].

Other leftovers: WindowsLatest cited additional lingering symptoms after the January 2026 update, including blank screens and Outlook Classic crashes, even as Microsoft shipped the emergency fixes [engadget.com#1].

Recent precedent: Microsoft previously issued an emergency Windows 11 fix in October for issues involving the Windows Recovery Environment, underscoring that out-of-band patches sometimes follow security releases [engadget.com#1].

perspectives.text: Microsoft: Microsoft described the shutdown/hibernate regression as affecting Windows 11 devices using Secure Launch and published a Known issues explanation for the remote sign-in failures tied to credential prompts, while delivering an out-of-band fix [engadget.com#1].

PC maintenance press: PCMag framed the incident as a Windows 11 bug that prevented some PCs from shutting down and pointed readers to Microsoft’s workaround/fix guidance for impacted Secure Launch systems [pcmag.com#1].

Independent Windows watchers: gHacks characterized the regressions as serious (shutdown/hibernate plus Remote Desktop) and emphasized that Microsoft’s emergency updates were intended to quickly reverse the breakage from the latest security patches [ghacks.net#1].

title: Update: Spain closes southern high-speed lines after crash
summary: Spanish authorities are investigating a deadly high-speed rail collision near Córdoba in southern Spain after one train derailed and ended up in the path of an oncoming service on Sunday evening [bbc.com#1][dw.com#1][theglobeandmail.com#1]. By Monday, officials reported at least 39 people killed and more than 120 injured, making it Spain’s worst rail accident in more than a decade [ft.com#1][dawn.com#1][euronews.com#2][aljazeera.com#3]. Services between Madrid and parts of Andalusia were suspended, and at least one report said the southern high-speed network faced wider closures as authorities worked at the scene and began safety checks [theguardian.com#1][nytimes.com#3].
quote: A night of deep pain for our country
talking_points: Who was onboard: Rail operator Adif said the Málaga-to-Madrid train carried about 300 passengers and the other service had roughly 200 onboard, underscoring the scale of the emergency response [theglobeandmail.com#1][rt.com#1][bbc.com#1].
Where it happened: The crash occurred near the municipality of Adamuz in Córdoba province at about 7:45 p.m. local time, according to Adif and multiple reports [scmp.com#1][dawn.com#1][rt.com#1].
Injuries and care: Emergency services in Andalusia said 122 people received treatment, with 48 still hospitalized and 12 in intensive care as of Monday morning [theguardian.com#1][scmp.com#1].

Investigation underway: Spain’s Railway Accident Investigation Commission opened an investigation, with officials saying the cause of the derailment was not immediately clear [theguardian.com#1][nytimes.com#2].

Why it puzzled: Transport Minister Óscar Puente said the derailment happened on a straight, recently renovated stretch of track and described the incident as “extremely strange” [dawn.com#1][ndtv.com#1][rt.com#1].

perspectives.text: Spanish transport minister Óscar Puente: He said the crash was hard to explain at this stage because it occurred on a straight, renovated section of track and involved a train that was “practically new,” while warning the death toll might still rise.

Rail infrastructure manager Adif: It reported the Málaga–Madrid train derailed near Adamuz and struck an oncoming Madrid–Huelva service, leading both trains to derail and prompting suspensions on the corridor.
Regional health authorities in Andalusia: They said rescue operations continued overnight, with the injured distributed across multiple hospitals as responders searched the wreckage for victims.

Witness/passenger (RTVE journalist Salvador Jimenez): He described the moment of impact as feeling “like an earthquake,” and later posted that passengers waited in the cold for buses to a sports center in Adamuz.

title: ISS microgravity drives phage evolution that boosts bacterial killing

Across time in orbit, genetic changes showed up on both sides of the arms race, affecting how phages latch onto bacteria and how bacteria defend themselves [sciencedaily.com#1]. Defense shifts: The bacteria also evolved, with genetic changes linked to defense against infection—evidence that resistance pressures continue in orbit, just along different evolutionary paths [sciencedaily.com#1].
